The Gommateshwara statue at Shravanabelagola (Karnataka) is a monolith, meaning it is carved out of a single, massive block of stone.

It is not built piece by piece. Instead, the entire 57-foot statue of Bahubali was sculpted from one solid granite rock.

This makes it one of the largest free-standing monolithic statues in the world.

Further Insights

The statue was commissioned in 981 CE by Chavundaraya under the Western Ganga dynasty.

It represents Bahubali in a meditative standing posture (Kayotsarga).

The Mahamastakabhisheka ceremony is held once every 12 years.

Monolithic architecture is also seen in rock-cut temples like Ellora.

Granite was chosen for durability and long-lasting preservation.

India has approximately 14,500 km of navigable inland waterways (rivers, canals, backwaters, creeks).

India's total coastline length (including island territories) is about 7,516 km.

National Waterway-1 (NW-1) runs along the Ganga - Bhagirathi - Hooghly river system from Prayagraj to Haldia.

NW-1 is developed under the Jal Marg Vikas Project.

Inland Water Transport (IWT) is more fuel-efficient and environmentally friendly compared to road transport.

NW-2 plays a key role in improving connectivity in Northeast India.

She defeated Tanvi Patri in a thrilling final, coming back from a game down to win.

Tanvi Patri lost the championship match to Surya Charishma Tamiri.

Vijayawada hosted the 87th edition in December 2025.

Surya Charishma's victory marked a significant career milestone for the young shuttler.

The championships also feature men's singles, doubles, and mixed doubles events.

Warli paintings, a traditional tribal art form from Maharashtra, use a distinctive white pigment made from rice paste.

The paste is prepared by:

Soaking and grinding rice

Mixing it with water and natural gum

This white pigment is then applied on a mud wall background using a bamboo stick.

Further Insights

Warli art originates from the Warli tribe of Maharashtra.

It uses simple geometric shapes: circles, triangles, and squares.

Themes include daily life, farming, hunting, and marriage rituals.

The central motif often includes the "Tarpa dance" scene.

Traditionally, Warli paintings were done on the walls of huts during special occasions.

The Konark Sun Temple (13th century CE, Odisha) and other medieval Indian temples used iron clamps, dowels, and beams to join massive stone blocks.

Instead of depending on mortar (like modern cement), the builders used:

Iron cramps (U-shaped clamps)

Iron dowels

Precision-cut interlocking stones

These methods improved structural stability, helping the monument withstand environmental stress,

Reason (R) is also true.

Archaeological studies and restoration work have confirmed that:

Stones were cut with extreme precision.

Iron dowels were inserted into carved sockets.

Blocks were interlocked mechanically.

Mortar was either minimally used or not relied upon structurally.

(R) correctly explains (A).

The use of iron dowels and interlocking stones explains how the structure achieved resilience and stability without mortar.

The mechanical locking system distributed weight effectively and added strength - which is why the structure remained stable.

Further Insights

Konark Sun Temple was built by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.

Iron beams used in Konark were highly corrosion-resistant due to ancient metallurgical skill.

Similar iron clamp techniques were used in Brihadeeswara Temple (Tamil Nadu).

Dry masonry (stone without mortar) was common in many Indian temples.

Interlocking architecture improves load distribution and reduces collapse risk.

The RISAT (Radar Imaging Satellite) series uses Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) technology. SAR is an active remote sensing system, meaning it sends its own microwave signals toward the Earth's surface and measures the reflected signals.

Microwave radiation has longer wavelengths compared to visible light. These waves can penetrate cloud cover, rain, and even work during night-time, since they do not depend on sunlight.

Further Insights

RISAT satellites are primarily used for surveillance, agriculture monitoring, and disaster management.

Microwave remote sensing is classified as active sensing, unlike optical remote sensing which is passive.

SAR can detect surface roughness, soil moisture, and even movement (Interferometric SAR).

RISAT-1 was developed by ISRO, while RISAT-2 had Israeli radar collaboration.

Radar wavelengths (like X-band, C-band) determine penetration depth and resolution.

The official theme for World Human Rights Day 2025 is "Human Rights, Our Everyday Essentials."

This theme highlights that human rights are not abstract ideals but the foundations of everyday life - like the rights to food, safety, freedom of expression, and dignity that we rely on each day

Further Insights

World Human Rights Day is observed every year on 10 December to mark the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1948.

The theme "Human Rights, Our Everyday Essentials" underscores that rights like dignity, freedom, and safety are part of daily life.

The theme aims to reconnect people with human rights that shape everyday experiences.

The day is used globally to raise awareness and inspire action toward protecting human rights.

Each year, the UN sets a specific theme to highlight a current focus area in human rights advocacy.

The MedaramJathara (also called Sammakka-Saralamma Jatara) is primarily celebrated by the Koya tribe in the state of Telangana.

It is a major tribal festival held biennially in Medaram village (Mulugu district). The festival honors tribal deities Sammakka and Saralamma, who are believed to have fought against unjust rulers to protect their people.

The Koya tribe plays a central role in conducting rituals, organizing ceremonies, and preserving the oral traditions associated with the festival.

Gond

The Gond tribe is one of the largest tribal communities in India, mainly found in central India (Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra),

Bhil

The Bhil tribe mainly resides in Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra.

Santhal

The Santhal tribe is concentrated in Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, and Bihar.

Further Insights

MedaramJathara is held once every two years (biennial festival).

It is recognized as a State Festival of Telangana.

The festival does not involve idol worship in the conventional sense; symbolic representations of deities are used.

It attracts crores of devotees, making it one of the largest religious gatherings in the world.

The Koya tribe belongs to the Dravidian tribal group and primarily inhabits Telangana, Chhattisgarh, and Andhra Pradesh.

Article 282 allows both the Union and the States to make grants for any public purpose, even if the subject is not within their legislative domain.

This Article forms the constitutional basis of Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) such as:

PMGSY

MGNREGA

National Health Mission

Even if a scheme relates to a State List subject (like public health or agriculture), the Union can still provide financial assistance under Article 282.

Article 263 deals with the Inter-State Council to resolve disputes and promote coordination.

Article 280 deals with the Finance Commission, which recommends distribution of taxes between Centre and States.

Article 312 deals with the creation of All India Services like IAS, IPS.

Further Insights

Centrally Sponsored Schemes are usually cost-shared between Centre and States.

Article 282 reflects India's model of cooperative federalism.

Finance Commission transfers (Article 280) are different from discretionary grants under Article 282.

CSS increased significantly after the Planning Commission era.

Article 275 also provides statutory grants to certain States.

A satellite that remains fixed over one point on the equator is in a Geostationary Orbit, not a Polar Orbit.

In a Polar Orbit, the satellite travels roughly from North Pole to South Pole while the Earth rotates beneath it. This allows the satellite to cover the entire Earth over time.

The North - South motion of a polar satellite is due to its orbital path being nearly perpendicular to the equator, not because of Earth's rotation.

The Earth's West - East rotation only helps different areas come under the satellite's path over time.

Further Insights

Polar orbits usually have an inclination close to 90 degrees.

Imaging and remote sensing satellites (like IRS, RISAT) use Sun-synchronous polar orbits.

Geostationary satellites orbit at about 36,000 km above the equator.

Polar satellites provide global coverage, while geostationary satellites provide continuous regional coverage.

Earth rotates from West to East, which allows polar satellites to scan new areas in each orbit.

"The Indian War of Independence 1857" was written by Vinayak Damodar Savarkar (V.D. Savarkar) and published in 1909.

The book was significant because:

It described the Revolt of 1857 as a planned national war of independence, not merely a "Sepoy Mutiny."

It promoted revolutionary nationalism.

The British government banned the book due to its anti-colonial tone.

It played an important role in shaping nationalist interpretation of the 1857 revolt.

Bal Gangadhar Tilak

Tilak wrote works like "Gita Rahasya" and was a strong nationalist leader

Further Insights

The British called it the Sepoy Mutiny, while Indian nationalists later termed it the First War of Independence.

The revolt began in Meerut on 10 May 1857.

After the revolt, the Government of India Act 1858 ended Company rule and began Crown rule.

The revolt saw participation of leaders like Rani Lakshmibai, Bahadur Shah Zafar, Tantia Tope.

Savarkar wrote the book while in London; it was secretly circulated in India.

Nitin Nabin has been appointed as the National Working President of the BJP and is the youngest person to hold this position in the party's history. His appointment represents a generational shift in the leadership of the party, reflecting a push towards involving younger leaders in top organisational roles.

Further Insights

The National Working President is a key organisational position responsible for party management and coordination.

Appointment of younger leaders aims to improve youth outreach and organisational dynamism.

Senior roles like National President and Working President are crucial in planning national election strategies.

The visible mushroom is just the fruiting body (reproductive structure) of a fungus.

The main organism actually exists underground (or inside wood/soil) as a network of thread-like structures called mycelium.

The mycelium can spread over a large area, while the mushroom we see is temporary and appears mainly for reproduction (spore dispersal).

Reason (R) - True

Some edible mushrooms are safe because they do not produce harmful toxins like certain poisonous fungi do (e.g., Amanita species).

However, fungi can sometimes accumulate heavy metals from soil, and toxicity depends on species and environment.

So broadly speaking, edible mushrooms are considered safe because they lack dangerous toxins present in poisonous species.

Further Insights (Fungi & Biology)

The largest living organism on Earth is a fungus (Armillaria), spread over several kilometers.

Mycelium plays a key role in nutrient recycling in ecosystems.

Some fungi form symbiotic relationships with plant roots (mycorrhiza).

Poisonous mushrooms like Amanita phalloides contain deadly toxins (amatoxins).

Fungi reproduce through spores, not seeds.

Sinapic acid is a naturally occurring phenolic compound derived from cinnamic acid. It is found in plants like mustard seeds, cereals, fruits, and vegetables.

It is known for:

Antioxidant properties (reduces oxidative stress)

Anti-inflammatory effects

Neuroprotective and antimicrobial potential

Reduces inflammation

Silappadikaram literally means "The Story (Adikaram) of the Anklet (Silambu)".

It is one of the Five Great Tamil Epics and was composed by Ilango Adigal. The story revolves around Kannagi, whose husband Kovalan is wrongly executed by the Pandya king. Kannagi proves his innocence by showing her anklet (silambu), which becomes the central symbol of justice and truth.

The epic highlights:

Moral justice

Role of women

Sangam-era trade and urban life

Political and social systems of ancient Tamilakam

Manimekalai

Manimekalai is another Tamil epic and is considered a sequel to Silappadikaram. It focuses on Buddhist philosophy and the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi.

Valayapathi

Valayapathi is one of the Five Great Tamil Epics, but much of it is lost. It is believed to have had Jain influence

CivakaCintamani

CivakaCintamani is a Jain epic that narrates the adventures of Jivaka (Civakan) and emphasizes ascetic ideals.

Further Insights

The Five Great Tamil Epics are: Silappadikaram, Manimekalai, CivakaCintamani, Valayapathi, and Kundalakesi.

Silappadikaram provides valuable details about Chola, Chera, and Pandya kingdoms.

Kannagi is revered as a symbol of chastity and justice in Tamil culture.

The epic reflects strong Jain influence, especially in its philosophical undertones.

It gives insights into ancient Tamil trade networks with Rome and Southeast Asia.

Two major discoveries in electromagnetism:

Hans Christian Ørsted (1820) discovered that an electric current flowing through a wire creates a magnetic field. He observed that a compass needle moved when placed near a current-carrying conductor.

Michael Faraday (1831) discovered electromagnetic induction - that a changing magnetic field (like a moving magnet) can produce an electric current in a conductor.

These discoveries form the foundation of modern electromagnetism and technologies like generators and transformers.

Further Insights

Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction is the basis of electric generators.

Ørsted's discovery linked electricity and magnetism for the first time.

James Clerk Maxwell later unified electricity and magnetism through Maxwell's equations.

Electromagnetism is one of the four fundamental forces of nature.

Modern power plants generate electricity using electromagnetic induction.

Under this scheme:

Investors deposit a lump sum.

They receive monthly interest payouts.

The principal amount is returned after 5 years.

It is a popular low-risk savings option backed by the Government of India.

Further Insights

POMIS provides monthly interest payouts, unlike many schemes that compound annually.

It is suitable for retirees seeking steady income.

The scheme has a maximum investment limit (separate limits for single and joint accounts).

Premature closure is allowed after 1 year with penalty conditions.

Interest rates are revised quarterly by the Government.

A pioneer of India's success in international tennis

The French Open is played on clay courts, which require strong baseline play.

India has historically performed better in doubles rather than singles at Grand Slams.

The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 officially replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973.

CrPC dealt with procedural aspects of criminal law, such as:

FIR registration

Arrest procedures

Investigation

Bail

Trial procedures

BNSS now governs all these procedural aspects of criminal justice in India.

Further Insights

The three new criminal laws came into force on 1 July 2024.

BNS replaces IPC (substantive criminal law).

BNSS replaces CrPC (criminal procedure).

BSA replaces the Indian Evidence Act (rules of evidence).

The 1918 Influenza pandemic caused millions of deaths in India. The British colonial government's response was widely seen as inadequate. At the same time:

Food shortages continued.

Grain exports were not effectively controlled.

Relief measures were insufficient.

This deepened public anger and contributed to growing distrust toward British rule. The crisis intensified anti-colonial sentiment, which later fed into movements like Non-Cooperation (1920).

Further Insights

The 1918 flu killed an estimated 12 - 18 million people in India.

Mahatma Gandhi himself contracted influenza during this period.

The crisis exposed weaknesses in colonial public health infrastructure.

The post-war period (1919 onwards) saw the Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh, intensifying nationalism.

Economic distress after World War I and the pandemic strengthened mass political mobilization.

He had a long literary career, and Naukar Ki Kameez is one of his best-known works.

Naukar Ki Kameez was adapted into a film by director Mani Kaul.

Shukla's writing style often combined everyday realism with poetic depth.

He also received the Sahitya Akademi Award earlier in his career.

His death was widely mourned across literary circles and public figures.

The Gini Coefficient does not measure total wealth.

It measures income or wealth inequality within a population. It shows how evenly (or unevenly) income is distributed.

A Gini value ranges from 0 to 1 (or sometimes expressed from 0 to 100).

0 = Perfect equality (everyone earns exactly the same income)

1 = Perfect inequality (one person has all the income)

Further Insights

The Gini Coefficient is derived from the Lorenz Curve.

A higher Gini value indicates greater inequality.

Nordic countries generally have low Gini values.

Developing economies often show higher inequality levels.

The Gini index does not capture absolute poverty - only distribution.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?

options.text: If it rains, we will cancel the picnic.
options.html: If it rains, we will cancel the picnic.

options.text: If it will rain, we cancel the picnic.
options.html: If it will rain, we cancel the picnic.

options.text: If it would rain, we will cancel the picnic.
options.html: If it would rain, we will cancel the picnic.

questions.solution:
The correct sentence is (a). This is first conditional for real future possibility: present simple in if-clause, "will" + base verb in main clause.

Option (b) is incorrect because if-clause uses present simple ("rains"), not future "will rain"; main clause should have "will."

Option (c) is incorrect as "would" implies second conditional (unreal), but here it's a real possibility.

Option (d) is incorrect mixing second ("would") and first ("will") conditionals inconsistently.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question: The figure of speech used in "The classroom was a fish market..."?
questions.questionHtml: The figure of speech used in "The classroom was a fish market..."?
questions.solution:
Option 1: A metaphor directly compares two different things by saying one is the other. In this case, the classroom is being compared to a zoo, implying noise, chaos, and disorder. No comparison words (like, as) are used, which makes it a metaphor.

Option 2: A simile compares two things using like or as. Example: "The classroom was like a zoo." Since the given line does not use like or as, it cannot be a simile.

Option 3: Hyperbole is an exaggeration used for emphasis. Example: "I'm so hungry I could eat a horse." The line "The classroom was a zoo" is not an exaggeration but a direct comparison, so it is not hyperbole.

Option 4: Alliteration is the repetition of initial consonant sounds in closely placed words. Example: "She sells seashells by the seashore." The sentence does not have repeated consonant sounds, so it is not alliteration.

Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Politeness is to do and say the kindest thing _____ the kindest way.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Politeness is to do and say the kindest thing _____ the kindest way.
questions.solution:
Such a preposition is to be used that can relate well the kindest thing with the kindest way. So, 'in' is the correct choice because here 'in' is used to express 'do and say' the kindest thing in the kindest way as an integral part of an activity, i.e., politeness. 'On' is used to express physically in contact with and supported by (a surface). 'To' is used to express motion in the direction of (a particular location). 'Of' is used to express the relationship between a part and a whole.

Hence, option (d) is correct.

Note:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

1) The teacher scolded the child for being late.

2) We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with an appropriate degree of comparison. The team that makes the ____________ mistakes will win the game.
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate degree of comparison.

The team that makes the ____________ mistakes will win the game.
questions.solution:
The sentence structure implies that one team is being singled out from a group (all the teams playing). It's the team that makes the minimum number of mistakes. This requires the superlative degree. The definite article "the" before the blank is a strong clue that a superlative is needed.

The blank modifies the noun "mistakes." "Mistakes" is a countable noun (you can have one mistake, two mistakes, etc.). The correct adjective for quantity with countable nouns is few.

The degrees of comparison for "few" are:

Positive: few

Comparative: fewer

Superlative: fewest

The complete sentence is: The team that makes the fewest mistakes will win the game.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Option a) few: This is the positive degree and does not show the necessary level of comparison.

Option b) fewer: This is the comparative degree, used to compare only two things (e.g., "This team made fewer mistakes than the other team"). The sentence implies a comparison among a larger group.

Option d) less: This is a very common grammar error. "Less" is the comparative form of "little" and is used for uncountable nouns (like time, sugar, or water). Since "mistakes" is a countable noun, the correct term is "fewer" (for comparative) or "fewest" (for superlative).

Note: · The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

Countable and uncountable nouns: 1. Countable nouns are the class of nouns that can be counted, for example, 'table' - one table, two tables, three tables, etc. 2. Uncountable nouns are the nouns that cannot be counted or usually are not counted, for example, light, water, milk, information, furniture, etc. They do not generally have a plural form and can't be preceded by 'a' or 'an'. Many abstract nouns are typically uncountable. Some uncountable nouns can be used in the plural as well, depending on the meaning or context of the word.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. He told me that he had accepted a new job offer with an exciting company in the city.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

He told me that he had accepted a new job offer with an exciting company in the city.

options.text: He said to me, "I have accepted a new job offer with an exciting company in the city."
options.html: He said to me, "I have accepted a new job offer with an exciting company in the city."

options.text: He said to me, "I will accept a new job offer with an exciting company in the city."

options.html: He said to me, "I will have accepted a new job offer with an exciting company in the city."

options.text: He says to me, "I accepted a new job offer with an exciting company in the city."
options.html: He says to me, "I accepted a new job offer with an exciting company in the city."

questions.solution:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense.

There are three cases when the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense.

· Tense remains same

· Past perfect changes to Present Perfect

· Past perfect changes to Simple Past

Case 1: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object) tense will be kept intact.

For example:

He said that he had just finished the movie. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I had just finished the movie" (Direct Speech)

Case 2: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object) will be converted into Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

Case 3: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object) will be converted into Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object).

For example:

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "Arya sent me a book" (Direct Speech)

As per the options, we have to go with Case 2.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

"Told me" will be changed to "said to me". "Says to me" will be incorrect, hence, option d) is eliminated.

"He had" will be changed to "I have".

Therefore, the correct answer is option a): He said to me, "I have accepted a new job offer with an exciting company in the city."

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech form of the following sentence. I said to him, "Let us get you up to the emergency care ward."
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the correct indirect speech form of the following sentence.

I said to him, "Let us get you up to the emergency care ward."

options.text: I asked him that we should get him to the emergency care ward.
options.html: I asked him that we should get him to the emergency care ward.

options.text: I ordered us to get him to the emergency care ward.
options.html: I ordered us to get him to the emergency care ward.

options.text: I suggested that they should get me to the emergency care ward.
options.html: I suggested that they should get me to the emergency care ward.

options.text: I suggested to him that we should get him up to the emergency care ward.
options.html: I suggested to him that we should get him up to the emergency care ward.

questions.solution:
Option (d) is the correct answer.

"Let" is used to mean "to allow" (request) or "to propose/suggest".

"Let" as a proposal/suggestion:

Rules to follow:

• "Said/said to" is changed to "proposed/proposed to" or "suggested/suggested to"

• 'That' is added in indirect speech.

• "Let" is removed in the indirect speech.

• The modal verb "should" is added in indirect speech.

• Pronouns 'us' and 'you' are changed into 'we' and 'him' respectively.

Example 1: He said, "Let us go to the amusement park." (Direct Speech)

He suggested that they should go to the amusement park. (Indirect Speech)

Example 2: I said to him, "Let us attend the office party." (Direct Speech)

I proposed to him that we should attend the office party. (Indirect Speech)

Therefore, the correct answer is: I suggested to him that we should get him up to the emergency care ward.
